summary.text: Marcela Mitaynes is the incumbent Democratic and Working Families Party candidate for NY State Assembly District 51 (Red Hook, Sunset Park and northern Bay Ridge). A tenant organizer who grew up in Sunset Park, she defeated a 26-year incumbent in the 2020 Democratic primary and has served since 2021; she is a member of the Banks, Children and Families, Education, Judiciary and Transportation committees and chairs the Subcommittee on Regulated Mortgage Lenders.

paragraphs.text: Migrated to New York City from Peru as a child and was raised in Sunset Park, Brooklyn, where she is raising her own family, according to her official Assembly biography.
Attended P.S. 169 in Sunset Park and later served as PTA president there when her own daughter attended the same school.
Wikipedia, citing the New York City Campaign Finance Board, lists an A.S. in Accounting from CUNY Kingsborough Community College.
Served on Brooklyn Community Board 7 for 10 years.

Was evicted from her rent-stabilized apartment of 30 years and, through her work with the tenant organizing group Neighbors Helping Neighbors, says she was instrumental in the passage of the 2019 Housing Stability and Tenant Protection Act, which strengthened rent-stabilized tenants' rights.

Ran for the Assembly for the first time in 2020. She defeated incumbent Felix Ortiz, who had represented the district since 1994, in the June 2020 Democratic primary after absentee ballots were counted; the Brooklyn Paper reported that she had endorsements from the Democratic Socialists of America and the Working Families Party and made housing reform her top issue.
Won the November 2020 general election and has represented the district since January 2021. She was re-elected in 2022 and 2024.

Current committee roles per the Assembly website: member of the Banks, Children and Families, Education, Judiciary and Transportation committees, and chair of the Subcommittee on Regulated Mortgage Lenders.

sources.title: Democratic socialist Marcela Mitaynes defeats 26-year incumbent in Sunset Park Assembly primary
